title: Meerut Conspiracy Case
definition: A landmark 1929 legal proceeding initiated by the British colonial government against 31 trade union leaders, communists, and activists, aimed at suppressing the rising influence of the Communist Party of India (CPI) and the organized labor movement.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the colonial state's repressive legislative response to the growth of socialist and communist ideologies in India, serving as a critical case study for the evolution of labor laws and civil liberties under the British Raj.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Meerut Conspiracy Case.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Growth of Trade Unionism in India
